mainTopic: The end of מומין אלו (vows על דעת רבים, נדר versus קבלה) and the opening משנה of the new perek on the two kinds of בכור: for inheritance and for the כהן
overview: This amud finishes the perek מומין אלו. A כהן who married a woman forbidden to him is made to take a נדר על דעת רבים. אמימר rules that such a vow cannot be undone, unless undoing it allows a מצוה, as the story of רב אחא, רבינא and the children's teacher shows. The גמרא then explains why a כהן who became טמא למתים only needs קבלה, while one who married in sin needs a נדר: his desire overpowers him. After the הדרן, a new perek opens with a משנה about four kinds of בכור: for inheritance, for the כהן, for both, or for neither. The משנה lists sons who are a firstborn for inheritance only, with רבי מאיר and חכמים disagreeing about miscarriages, and רבי יוסי הגלילי disagreeing about converts. It then lists sons who are a firstborn for the כהן but not for inheritance.

steps.title: The vow is made on the consent of the public
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the earlier statement: the כהן who married in sin is made to vow על דעת רבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We make him vow] on the consent of the public.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a sentence from before. The כהן who married a forbidden woman is made to take his vow על דעת רבים, which is a vow tied to the consent of the public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow made על דעת רבים is extra strong, because it depends on many people agreeing. This sets up אמימר's ruling in the next step about whether such a vow can ever be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: On the consent of the public, a vow tied to the agreement of many people
We make him take a vow

phrases.english: him, on the consent of the public.
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence from before: we make the כהן who married in sin take his vow based on the public's consent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the statement that runs over from the earlier text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vow of the כהן who married in sin is made על דעת רבים.

steps.title: אמימר: a vow on the public's consent cannot be undone
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that a vow made על דעת רבים cannot be undone, even according to the view that a public vow can be.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: The הלכה is that even according to the one who says a vow made in public can be undone, a vow made on the consent of the public cannot be undone.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives a final halacha. A vow that is tied to the public's consent cannot be undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of vow here. One is a vow made in front of many people (ברבים), and the other is a vow that depends on their consent (על דעת רבים). There is an opinion that even a public vow can be undone, but אמימר says everyone agrees the second kind cannot be undone, since you would need all those people to agree.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow made in front of many people

steps.confusionAlert: 'בָּרַבִּים' (in front of many people) and 'עַל דַּעַת הָרַבִּים' (depending on their consent) sound alike, but they are two different things. Only the second cannot be undone according to everyone.

phrases.english: Ameimar said: The halakha is:
even according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: נֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר בָּרַבִּים יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה,
phrases.english: a vow that was taken in public can be undone,

phrases.aramaic: עַל דַּעַת הָרַבִּים אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה.
phrases.english: one taken on the consent of the public cannot be undone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how strong the vow in step 1 is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow made על דעת רבים cannot be undone, according to everyone.

steps.title: Limit: a vow can be undone for the sake of a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The rule only applies when undoing the vow would allow something optional. If it would allow a מצוה, the vow can be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to an optional matter, but for a matter of a מצוה it can be undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits אמימר's rule. Even a vow made על דעת רבים can be undone when undoing it allows a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This does not cancel the category of a vow על דעת רבים. It adds an exception: the need for a מצוה is strong enough to allow it to be undone. If undoing the vow would only allow something optional, the vow stays in force.

phrases.english: And this applies to an optional matter,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה.
phrases.english: but for a matter of a מצוה it can be undone.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow על דעת רבים can be undone in order to allow a מצוה.

steps.title: The story of the children's teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא made a teacher vow to stop teaching. רבינא undid the vow because no other teacher was as careful as he was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like that teacher of children: רב אחא made him vow because he was negligent with the children, and רבינא brought him back, because they did not find anyone as careful as him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that shows the exception in action. Teaching children תורה is a מצוה, so the vow was undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא made the teacher vow על דעת רבים to stop teaching, because he was too rough with the children. That would normally make the vow impossible to undo. Still, רבינא undid it, because the children needed the best teacher, and this is a מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: A vow על דעת רבים normally cannot be undone, but it can be undone when this allows a מצוה, such as teaching children.

phrases.english: As in the case of a certain teacher of children,
Rav Aḥa made him vow [to stop teaching]
because he was negligent with the children,
phrases.notes: He was hitting the children too much.

phrases.english: and Ravina brought him back,
because he did not find anyone who was as careful as him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the exception for a מצוה.
steps.raayaObject: A vow על דעת רבים may be undone for the sake of a מצוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב אחא, רבינא and the teacher

steps.title: Why the טמא כהן only needs to accept upon himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a כהן who became טמא למתים only needs קבלה, while one who married in sin needs a נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who becomes טמא for the dead...' Why is it enough here for him to accept upon himself, while there we make him take a vow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to another case in the משנה and compares two cases. It asks why one needs only a commitment while the other needs a full vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are כהנים who did something forbidden and need to show they will stop. The טמא כהן only accepts upon himself, but the one who married in sin is made to take a vow. The גמרא wants to know what the difference is.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן who makes himself טמא through the dead
Accepting a commitment upon himself, without a vow

phrases.english: 'And one who becomes impure for the dead,' etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: he may not serve until he accepts upon himself that he will stop.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּקַבָּלָה,
phrases.english: What is different here, that acceptance is enough for him,
and what is different there, that we make him take a vow?
phrases.notes: 'There' means the כהן who married a woman forbidden to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּקַבָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה and compares it with the case discussed above.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why there is a different requirement for the טמא כהן and for the one who married in sin

steps.title: There his desire overpowers him
steps.stepSummary: The person who married in sin is driven by a strong desire, so a stronger commitment is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Desire for a woman is very strong, so a simple promise is not enough and a נדר is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Becoming טמא is not driven by a powerful urge, so accepting upon himself is enough. A forbidden marriage is driven by a strong יצר, so the חכמים require a binding vow to hold him back.
steps.whatToRemember: How strong the commitment must be depends on how strong the temptation is. A strong desire calls for a נדר.

phrases.english: There, his desire overpowers him.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forbidden marriage is driven by a strong desire, so a vow is required.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing מומין אלו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of the perek מומין אלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, מומין אלו.
steps.whatsHappening: This line ends the perek. It is a traditional farewell to the chapter we just finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן marks the end of a perek and shows our wish to come back and learn it again. The next perek starts a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of the perek, 'These blemishes'

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'These blemishes.'

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The perek מומין אלו is finished.

steps.title: New perek: four kinds of firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the new perek by listing four possibilities: firstborn for נחלה only, for the כהן only, for both, or for neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a son who is a firstborn for inheritance but not for the כהן; one who is a firstborn for the כהן but not for inheritance; one who is a firstborn for both; and one who is a firstborn for neither.
steps.whatsHappening: A new perek begins. The משנה sets out four categories of 'firstborn' that it will explain one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בכור' is really two separate statuses. One is about the double portion of inheritance (נחלה). The other is about פדיון הבן, redeeming the son from the כהן. Because they are separate, a son can have one without the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (marks the start of the משנה text)
A firstborn who gets the double share of the father's inheritance
A firstborn who must be redeemed from a כהן (פדיון הבן)
Redeeming a firstborn son by paying a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole perek is built on this four-part list. Each later case fits into one of these boxes.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume 'בכור' always means one thing. Here it means two separate statuses, and they don't always go together.

phrases.english: MISHNA: There is a firstborn for inheritance,
who is not a firstborn for the priest;
phrases.notes: 'For the priest' means he would need פדיון הבן, being redeemed from a כהן.

phrases.english: a firstborn for the priest who is not a firstborn for inheritance;
a firstborn for both inheritance and the priest;
and there is one who is not a firstborn
neither for inheritance nor for the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new perek after the הדרן of מומין אלו in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Firstborn status for נחלה and firstborn status for the כהן are separate, giving four possible combinations.

steps.title: Firstborn for inheritance only: רבי מאיר's cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts explaining the first category. A son born after a non-viable baby, a stillborn, or an animal-shaped miscarriage is a firstborn for נחלה but not for the כהן, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which son is a firstborn for inheritance but not for the כהן? One born after non-viable babies, even if that baby's head came out alive; or after a full nine-month baby whose head came out dead; or after the mother miscarried something shaped like a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks which son fits the first category, then answers with a list of cases. The list is רבי מאיר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case something already came out of the mother's womb before this son, so he is not the first to 'open the womb' and needs no פדיון. But the earlier birth was not a living son to the father, so this son is still the father's firstborn for inheritance. רבי מאיר counts even an animal-shaped miscarriage as opening the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: Domestic animal, wild animal, and bird

steps.confusionAlert: 'Even though its head came out alive' is about the earlier non-viable baby, not about the son we are discussing.

phrases.english: Which one is a firstborn for inheritance
but is not a firstborn for the priest?
One who comes after non-viable babies,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיָּצָא אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ חַי,
phrases.english: even though that baby's head came out alive,
or after a nine-month baby whose head came out dead,
or a son of a woman who miscarried something like a domestic animal, wild animal, or bird
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזֶהוּ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the four categories from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a son born after non-viable babies, a stillborn, or an animal-shaped miscarriage is a firstborn for נחלה but not for the כהן.

steps.title: חכמים: the miscarriage must have a human form
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר about the animal-shaped miscarriage. It only cancels the next son's פדיון if it has some human form.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: the miscarriage does not count unless it has some human form.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים give a different opinion on רבי מאיר's last case, the animal-shaped miscarriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, an animal-shaped miscarriage counts as opening the womb, so the next son needs no פדיון. For חכמים it counts only if it has some human features. Without that, the next son is still a firstborn for the כהן.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
not unless it has some human form.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the animal-shaped miscarriage in רבי מאיר's list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's animal-shaped miscarriage case in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal-shaped miscarriage cancels the next son's פדיון only if it has some human form.

steps.title: More cases: sandal, afterbirth, sac, baby in pieces
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds more cases. A son born after a 'sandal' miscarriage, an afterbirth, a sac with formed tissue, or a baby that came out in pieces is a firstborn for נחלה but not for the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman miscarried a 'sandal', or an afterbirth, or a sac with formed tissue, or a baby that came out in pieces, the son born after them is a firstborn for inheritance but not for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of sons who are a firstborn for inheritance only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these things already came out of the womb, so the next son is not the first to open it and needs no פדיון. None was a living son to the father, so the next son still gets the firstborn's inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: A gestational sac with formed tissue

phrases.english: A woman who miscarries a sandal,
phrases.notes: A 'sandal' is a flat, fish-shaped fetus.

phrases.english: or an afterbirth, or a sac with formed tissue,
or a baby that comes out in pieces
the son who comes after them is a firstborn for inheritance,
but is not a firstborn for the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפֶּלֶת סַנְדָּל, אוֹ שִׁלְיָא, אוֹ שַׁפִּיר מְרוּקָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the חכמים's statement from step 10, adding more cases that, like רבי מאיר's list in step 9, make the next son a firstborn for inheritance only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son born after a sandal, afterbirth, formed sac, or baby in pieces is a firstborn for נחלה but not for the כהן.

steps.title: Mother who gave birth before: earlier marriage, maidservant, or convert
steps.stepSummary: A man with no sons marries a woman who already gave birth, or who gave birth while still a שפחה or a נכרית. Her son born after she joined ישראל is a firstborn for נחלה but not for the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man had no sons and married a woman who had already given birth, or who gave birth while still a maidservant and was later freed, or while still a non-Jew and later converted. When she gave birth after joining ישראל, the son is a firstborn for inheritance but not for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its list with cases where the mother already had a child before this son, so only the inheritance status remains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the father has no earlier sons, so this son is his firstborn for inheritance. But the mother already gave birth earlier, so this son did not open her womb and needs no פדיון. This holds even if the earlier birth was while she was a שפחה or a נכרית.
steps.whatToRemember: Firstborn for the כהן depends on the mother: was this son the first to open her womb? Firstborn for inheritance depends on the father: is this his first son? When the mother already gave birth but the father has no sons, the son is a firstborn for נחלה only.

phrases.english: One who had no sons,
and he married a woman who had already given birth,
or who gave birth while still a maidservant and was then freed,
or while still a non-Jew and then converted,
and once she joined Israel she gave birth to a son
he is a firstborn for inheritance but not a firstborn for the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים, וְנָשָׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁכְּבָר יָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another group of cases to the first category from step 8, this time about the mother's earlier births.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the mother already gave birth, even as a שפחה or נכרית, her son born after joining ישראל to a man with no sons is a firstborn for נחלה but not for the כהן.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: a son born after conversion is a full firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees with the case in step 12. He holds that the son is a בכור for both נחלה and the כהן, because births that happened before the mother joined ישראל do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: he is a firstborn for inheritance and for the כהן, as it says 'opening the womb in ישראל', meaning only once they open the womb as part of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי argues with the case we just learned: a woman gave birth while she was a נכרית or a שפחה, and then had a son after joining ישראל. He says this son counts as a בכור for everything, including the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said the earlier birth 'used up' the opening of her womb, so this son is not a בכור for the כהן. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the words 'בישראל' to mean that only a womb-opening that happens while she is Jewish counts. So the births from before she was Jewish are ignored, and this son is the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees here with the first opinion of the משנה
The first baby to open the mother's womb
'In Israel': he learns from this that the birth must happen while the mother is Jewish
A firstborn both for the double share of inheritance and for פדיון הבן

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, births from before a woman became Jewish do not count. Her first son born after she joined ישראל is a full בכור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
he is a firstborn for inheritance and for the priest,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the son from step 12, born after his mother joined ישראל.

phrases.english: as it says: "opening the womb in Israel"
meaning: only once they open the womb as part of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion on the last case of the first category.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son born after his mother converted or was freed is a בכור for both נחלה and the כהן, since only births 'in Israel' count.

steps.title: Firstborn for the כהן but not for inheritance: father already had sons, or mother converted or was freed while pregnant
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts the second category: the son is the first from his mother's womb, but not the first son of his father for inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man who already had sons married a woman who had never given birth, or a woman converted while pregnant, or a maidservant was freed while pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves to a new category: a son who is a בכור for the כהן but not for נחלה. It lists the first cases, and the ruling for them comes at the end of step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פדיון הבן depends on the mother: was this the first baby to open her womb? The double inheritance depends on the father: is this his first son? In the first case the father already has older sons. In the other two cases the baby was conceived before his mother joined ישראל, so he is not counted as his father's son for inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: A maidservant who was freed while pregnant

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of בכור. The כהן side follows the mother's womb, and the inheritance side follows the father.

phrases.english: One who had sons
and married a woman who had not given birth,
or a woman who converted while pregnant,
or a maidservant who was freed while pregnant.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים וְנָשָׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁלֹּא יָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the second category listed in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These sons are a בכור for the כהן but not for נחלה (the ruling is stated in step 16).

steps.title: Babies mixed up at birth
steps.stepSummary: An Israelite woman gave birth at the same time as a כהן's wife, a לויה, or a woman who already gave birth, and it is not known which baby belongs to which mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she gave birth together with a כהנת, or with a לויה, or with a woman who had already given birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds more cases to the second category: babies who got mixed up at birth, so nobody knows which mother each one belongs to. The ruling still comes at the end of step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each pair, the other mother's son would not need פדיון from a כהן. Because of the mix-up, the child is treated as a בכור for the כהן. But since it is unclear who his father is, he cannot prove he is anyone's firstborn son, so he does not get the double share of inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter or wife of a כהן
The daughter or wife of a לוי
Who had already given birth before

phrases.english: and if she gave birth together with a kohen's wife,
phrases.notes: An Israelite woman and another woman give birth together, and the babies get mixed up.

phrases.english: or she and a Levite woman,
or she and a woman who had already given birth,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases to the second category.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed-up babies are a בכור for the כהן but not for נחלה (the ruling is stated in step 16).

steps.title: Unknown father after a quick remarriage, and the ruling for the whole category
steps.stepSummary: A woman remarried within three months of leaving her first husband and gave birth, and it is unknown which husband is the father. In all these cases the son is a בכור for the כהן but not for נחלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise a woman who did not wait three months after her husband, then married and gave birth, and it is unknown whether the baby is a nine-month baby of the first husband or a seven-month baby of the second. In all these cases he is a firstborn for the כהן but not a firstborn for inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one last case, a baby whose father is uncertain. Then it states the ruling for every case since step 14: he is a בכור for the כהן but not for inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is clear the baby opened his mother's womb, so he is a בכור for the כהן. But a baby can be born after nine months or after seven months, so either husband could be the father. Since no one can prove who his father is, he cannot claim the double share from either one.

keyTerms.meaning: Three months, the waiting time before remarrying
A baby born after nine months of pregnancy
A baby born after seven months of pregnancy

steps.whatToRemember: Second category: whenever the baby is clearly the first from his mother but is not (or cannot be proven to be) his father's first son, he is a בכור for the כהן but not for נחלה.

phrases.english: And likewise a woman who did not wait
three months after her husband
phrases.notes: He means after her first husband died or divorced her.

phrases.english: and she married and gave birth,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ אִם בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה לָרִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: and it is not known whether he is a nine-month baby of the first husband
or a seven-month baby of the second husband
he is a firstborn for the priest but not a firstborn for inheritance.
phrases.notes: This ruling covers every case from step 14 until here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last case and states the ruling for the whole second category.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In all these cases the son is a בכור for the כהן but not for the double inheritance share.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being a בכור for the כהן and being a בכור for inheritance are two separate questions, and one can be true without the other.
